O.outcome_detail: perceived visual and tactile realism, including tissue differentiation

result.effect: Over 80% of HVRS participants selected agree or strongly agree on SP2-SP4; no printed between-group effect size

cells.quote: When completing the survey, participants in the HVRS group showed notably higher levels of agreement on items related to realism, motor skill development and confidence. Specifically, items SP2, SP3 and SP4, which addressed visual realism, tissue differentiation and tactile feedback, received predominantly positive responses in the HVRS group, with over 80% of participants selecting ‘agree’ or ‘strongly agree’.
cells.note: This is a self-reported survey outcome. Participants had prior paediatric dentistry and preclinical training but no experience using haptic virtual reality simulation in primary teeth.

O.outcome_detail: drilling time for pulpotomy access preparation

result.effect: HVRS-first subsequent laboratory session: mean 198.4 s (SD = 65.7); LAB-first initial session: mean 264.7 s (SD = 72.3)

cells.quote: Students who began their training with the haptic virtual reality simulator demonstrated greater efficiency in the subsequent laboratory session, completing the task in a reduced average time of 198.4 s (SD = 65.7). In contrast, those who started with the conventional laboratory model required more time during their initial session (mean = 264.7 s; SD = 72.3) and exhibited only a modest reduction in performance time when transitioning to the simulator.
cells.note: Participants were fourth-year dental students with prior structured paediatric dentistry and preclinical training, but no experience using HVRS in primary teeth. The study reports means but no significance test or power/equivalence evidence for the timing comparison, so direction is coded ns.
